about infinite hill

infinite hill is a lesson a day in the religion you grew up in — or the one you're curious about — read to you by people you already listen to, and checked by people who actually know.

eight doors: Christianity, Catholicism, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism — and my own path, if none of them. one house. you don't need a religion to come in. change it anytime. walk two.

why we're doing this

for five thousand years every people on earth built the same thing: a way to sit down, get quiet, and remember what matters. different names, same tool. in one generation, a lot of us let it go, and a feed moved into the space it left. it doesn't have to stay that way.

the world's loud. everyone's certain, nobody's calm. and machines are starting to do a lot of the work we used to define ourselves by. when the work changes, who are you? every generation before us had somewhere to sit with that question. we can have one too.

what we're for

a generation that grows up less alone and more grounded than the one before it. peace and love — not as a slogan, as a habit. and one rule under all of it: treat people the way you want to be treated. every religion on earth arrived at it on its own. nobody's ever beaten it. the golden rule is undefeated.

two doors, one table

four in ten new marriages in America are between faiths. the kids in those houses grow up with two calendars, two sets of holidays, two sets of prayers — and usually end up with none, because nobody built a place that holds both. we did. one house, eight doors, and you can walk two. the house that does Christmas and Hanukkah — or Diwali and Eid, or whichever pair is yours. nobody has to pick a side at dinner.

the six things we'll never do

we don't pick your door. we care that you have one. we don't compare. we don't guilt. we don't write your prayers. we don't sell your faith.

who we are

a small team in Los Angeles. we're a company, not a church, and we're not affiliated with any religious institution. the people who keep us honest are the Keepers. the people who read to you are the voices. we write, they check, they read. that's the whole machine.

a note from the founder

My mom walked ten thousand steps a day. Then, in late 2025, she got sick — and two weeks later she was gone. I wasn't ready. Nobody was.

Her name was Usha Kiran — a ray of the morning sun. She was an elementary school teacher who never lost the language of children, and her last words to her ten grandchildren were "to infinity and beyond."

At her funeral I watched my son's face. He's autistic, and I had been the one to explain to him where she went. The look on him when he understood she wasn't coming back is the thing that shattered me.

A few months later I went on my first silent retreat. Days of nothing. What I found at the bottom of it was that faith — the quiet, unfashionable thing my mom had handed me without ever forcing it — was what had been holding me up the whole time. It held my family up too. We didn't get through those weeks on willpower. We got through them on something older.

Then I looked around. A generation lost in the scroll — more connected and lonelier than any before it — and not one of us prepared for the one fact coming for all of us: this ends. Every generation before us had a way to sit with that. We threw it out in one generation and replaced it with a feed.

infinite hill is my attempt to change how that goes. To hand the oldest tools on earth to the next generation the way they were handed to me — without pressure, in a voice they'd actually listen to, through whichever door is theirs. We don't care which door. We care that you have one.

The sun on every screen is for her. To infinity and beyond.

— Shaan
